S28(c) - the ruling requires a re-cut leg be re-verified against the full water census, the slope histogram and reachability. The builder re-timed only. I ran the rest at HEAD: road-water-audit 0 leg/phase offences over 4 phases x 10 legs; scale-audit S9-NO-FENCES 13/13 regions and 8/8 settlements; M36-ROAD-RELIEF 31.8%; M4 worst leg 2.26%; crossing 57.59 min. All PASS - so (c) holds in fact but was never checked by the piece.

The ridge argument: the CONCLUSION is right and the EVIDENCE does not support it. critic-road-join-ridge.mjs finds the joined and pre-join roads 0.21 m apart AT THE STALL (worst 2.03 m in the 120 m window), which settles it. But the builder's "over the same metres" is false: 63.7% of stormhold-helstrom moved >1 m (worst 17.91) and 95% of helstrom-blackrose (worst 67.43). And the stated CAUSE is an artefact - bare-field ground at the stall is 26.57 deg, not 57.5/61.09. W1-CROSSING found the same independently: 918 m of that leg is bridge and the body was 15.3 m BELOW the road.

Two slope regressions the join caused and nobody recorded: blackrose-lilmoth centreline 39.66 -> 40.41 deg, putting 1 m of trunk road over the 40 deg walkable limit; helstrom-blackrose worst skirt at +/-5.6 m 30.27 -> 39.72 deg and centreline 29.04 -> 37.22 deg. Both are what S28(c)'s slope histogram exists to surface.

My own consumption, 6 arms: R-REMEDY rebuild at HEAD -> 0 of 10 (the mechanism is sound, the artefact is stale); R-DETERM byte-identical; TEARDOWN --no-join 10 of 10 / 267 samples with a distinct hash (I watched my own control go red, rule 6); P-BLACKROSE bites 19 samples from 11 and follows to 0 with the road moving 5.5 m in a town the builder never perturbed; NULL-NOREAD byte-identical roads.json; NULL-REVERSED the x6 grow SURVIVED the shrink pass at HEAD, so the per-axis shrink is more permissive than the one the builder measured against.
